question.problem:
Solve the following congruence:

$$
9x-22≡7\,(\text{mod}\,11)
$$

*Hint: You may wish to use trial and error to find the appropriate multiplicative inverse.*
question.worked_solution:
First, we reduce our congruence to a congruence of the form $ax≡b,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}9x-22 & ≡7\, & (\text{mod}\,11) \\ 9x-22+22 & ≡7+22\, & (\text{mod}\,11) \\ 9x & ≡29\, & (\text{mod}\,11) \\ 9x & ≡2\cdot 11+7\, & (\text{mod}\,11) \\ 9x & ≡7\, & (\text{mod}\,11)\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that a linear congruence $ax≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)$ has a unique solution modulo $n$ if and only if $\text{gcd}(a,n)=1.$

In the given congruence, we have $a=9$ and $n=11$, and

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(9,11)=1.
$$

So, our congruence does indeed have a unique solution.

To find the solution, we need to multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $9\,(\text{mod}\,11).$ To find the inverse of $9\,(\text{mod}\,11)$, we compute the exponents of $9\,(\text{mod}\,11)$ until we get a result of $1\,(\text{mod}\,11):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{9}^{2} & ≡81≡7\cdot 11+4≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,11) \\ {9}^{3} & ≡4\cdot 9≡36≡3\cdot 11+3≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,11) \\ {9}^{4} & ≡3\cdot 9≡27≡2\cdot 11+5≡5 &  & (\text{mod}\,11) \\ {9}^{5} & ≡5\cdot 9≡45≡4\cdot 11+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,11)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $5\cdot 9≡1\,(\text{mod}\,11),$ which means that $5$ is the multiplicative inverse of $9$ (modulo $11$).

Now, multiplying both sides of our congruence by $5,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}9x & ≡7 &  & (\text{mod}\,11) \\ 5\cdot 9x & ≡5\cdot 7 &  & (\text{mod}\,11) \\ (5\cdot 9)x & ≡35 &  & (\text{mod}\,11) \\ 1\cdot x & ≡2+3\cdot 11 &  & (\text{mod}\,11) \\ x & ≡2 &  & (\text{mod}\,11)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x≡2\,(\text{mod}\,11).$
